subject: history_social
passage: The Crystal Palace, built in London's Hyde Park to house the Great Exhibition of 1851, was designed not by an architect but by Joseph Paxton, a gardener who had made his reputation constructing greenhouses of iron and glass. His design succeeded where more than two hundred competition entries had failed largely because of a quality that had little to do with beauty: nearly every part of the building, from its cast-iron columns to its panes of glass, was made to a few standard sizes and could be produced in quantity at factories and bolted together on site. ______ the building was conceived less as a monument than as a kit, assembled from interchangeable pieces.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The second sentence explains in detail that the building's parts came in standard sizes, were made in factories, and were bolted together on site. The last sentence sums up that same idea in a single image: the building was a kit. A restatement transition is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Specifically" would introduce a narrower, more detailed point, but the last sentence is a broader summary of the detail that came before. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The idea of a kit is not one example of standardized parts; it describes the whole building's design.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals something true despite the previous point, but calling the building a kit agrees with the description of standard, bolted parts. It is tempting because the kit image seems to downplay the building's grandeur.
explanation.D: Correct. "In other words" signals that the last sentence restates the point about standardized, factory-made parts as the idea of a kit.
